statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r has no repeated entries and, for every person p with 0 <= p < n, p occurs in r if and only if p belongs to the final secret set K defined as follows. Let K_0 = {0, firstPerson}. Process the distinct meeting times in increasing order. For a time t, let G_t be the undirected graph on people {0,...,n-1} with an edge between x and y exactly when meetings contains a triple [x,y,t] or [y,x,t]. Let K_<t be the set obtained after processing all times less than t. Let C_t be the union of all connected components of G_t (including isolated vertices) that contain at least one vertex of K_<t. Set K_t = K_<t union C_t. Then K is the set after processing the largest meeting time (and K = K_0 if meetings is empty). The entries of r may be in any order.
preconditions: 2 <= n <= 10^5; 1 <= len(meetings) <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < len(meetings), len(meetings[i]) = 3, and if meetings[i] = [x_i, y_i, t_i] then 0 <= x_i, y_i <= n-1, x_i != y_i, and 1 <= t_i <= 10^5; 1 <= firstPerson <= n-1.

statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail, panic, overflow, or access out of bounds) for every input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: 2 <= n <= 10^5; 1 <= len(meetings) <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < len(meetings), len(meetings[i]) = 3, and if meetings[i] = [x_i, y_i, t_i] then 0 <= x_i, y_i <= n-1, x_i != y_i, and 1 <= t_i <= 10^5; 1 <= firstPerson <= n-1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every index i with 0 <= i < len(r), the integer r[i] satisfies 0 <= r[i] < n.
preconditions: 2 <= n <= 10^5; 1 <= len(meetings) <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < len(meetings), len(meetings[i]) = 3, and if meetings[i] = [x_i, y_i, t_i] then 0 <= x_i, y_i <= n-1, x_i != y_i, and 1 <= t_i <= 10^5; 1 <= firstPerson <= n-1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for all indices i and j with 0 <= i < j < len(r), r[i] != r[j].
preconditions: 2 <= n <= 10^5; 1 <= len(meetings) <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < len(meetings), len(meetings[i]) = 3, and if meetings[i] = [x_i, y_i, t_i] then 0 <= x_i, y_i <= n-1, x_i != y_i, and 1 <= t_i <= 10^5; 1 <= firstPerson <= n-1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every index i with 0 <= i < len(meetings), writing meetings[i] = [x,y,t], if x = 0 or x = firstPerson then y occurs in r, and if y = 0 or y = firstPerson then x occurs in r.
preconditions: 2 <= n <= 10^5; 1 <= len(meetings) <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < len(meetings), len(meetings[i]) = 3, and if meetings[i] = [x_i, y_i, t_i] then 0 <= x_i, y_i <= n-1, x_i != y_i, and 1 <= t_i <= 10^5; 1 <= firstPerson <= n-1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every person p that occurs in r there exist an integer k >= 0, people p_0,...,p_k, and meeting times t_1,...,t_k such that p_k = p, p_0 = 0 or p_0 = firstPerson, and for every j with 1 <= j <= k, meetings contains a meeting whose two endpoints are p_{j-1} and p_j and whose time is t_j, and 1 <= t_1 <= t_2 <= ... <= t_k. When k = 0 this says p is 0 or firstPerson.
preconditions: 2 <= n <= 10^5; 1 <= len(meetings) <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < len(meetings), len(meetings[i]) = 3, and if meetings[i] = [x_i, y_i, t_i] then 0 <= x_i, y_i <= n-1, x_i != y_i, and 1 <= t_i <= 10^5; 1 <= firstPerson <= n-1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every person p with 0 <= p < n, if there exist an integer k >= 0, people p_0,...,p_k, and meeting times t_1,...,t_k such that p_k = p, p_0 = 0 or p_0 = firstPerson, for every j with 1 <= j <= k meetings contains a meeting whose two endpoints are p_{j-1} and p_j and whose time is t_j, and 1 <= t_1 <= t_2 <= ... <= t_k, then p occurs in r.
preconditions: 2 <= n <= 10^5; 1 <= len(meetings) <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < len(meetings), len(meetings[i]) = 3, and if meetings[i] = [x_i, y_i, t_i] then 0 <= x_i, y_i <= n-1, x_i != y_i, and 1 <= t_i <= 10^5; 1 <= firstPerson <= n-1.

statement: Whenever the function returns r on input (n, meetings, firstPerson) and returns r' on input (n, meetings', firstPerson), for every person p with 0 <= p < n, p occurs in r if and only if p occurs in r'.
preconditions: 2 <= n <= 10^5; 1 <= firstPerson <= n-1; meetings and meetings' are two valid meeting arrays, meaning each has length between 1 and 10^5, each entry has length 3, and for each meeting [x,y,t] in either array, 0 <= x,y <= n-1, x != y, and 1 <= t <= 10^5; and for every time t and every unordered pair of distinct people {x,y}, some meeting [x,y,t] or [y,x,t] occurs in meetings if and only if some meeting [x,y,t] or [y,x,t] occurs in meetings'.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every time t and every pair of people x,y with 0 <= x,y < n, if x belongs to K_<t and x and y lie in the same connected component of the undirected graph H_t, then y occurs in r. Here K_<t is the set of people who know the secret after all meetings with time strictly less than t, computed from K_0 = {0, firstPerson} by, for each meeting time t' < t in increasing order, adding every vertex in a connected component of H_{t'} that contains a vertex already in the set; and H_t is the undirected graph on {0,...,n-1} whose edges are {a,b} for every meeting [a,b,t] or [b,a,t] in meetings.
preconditions: 2 <= n <= 10^5; 1 <= len(meetings) <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < len(meetings), len(meetings[i]) = 3, and if meetings[i] = [x_i, y_i, t_i] then 0 <= x_i, y_i <= n-1, x_i != y_i, and 1 <= t_i <= 10^5; 1 <= firstPerson <= n-1.
